The moment I'm going to invite my neighbor to come to anything, the devil is right there. My heart is pounding. It's nerve-wracking. That is the moment where you know, wow, this is right. If Satan doesn't want me to do this, I'm probably doing something right. And that's where you just gotta pray that the Holy Spirit would guide you and give you power and courage, and you just take that step. And you let Jesus do the rest. It doesn't have to be smooth. It just has to be an initiative. It just needs to be a question. Will you come to church with me during this Easter? Lastly, while the light of the lamp is both for us and others to see, notice how our jobs have nothing to do with the light itself. We don't maintain it. We don't cause the fire to keep going. No, that happens on its own. The light of the lamp is what gives light. And that's not us. That's God. That's God. That's Jesus in us. That's the Holy Spirit working to purify us. And praise God that it is his work and not all Brothers and sisters, this light will never run out. Think about the scene of Moses encountering the burning bush. Moses encounters a bush that is on fire, but is not consumed. That fire burned on the bush, yet did not consume it. It was sustained by supernatural power. Likewise, the light that is in you is sustained by supernatural power. It will enable you to accomplish what you have been designed to do. And so shine so that others might be restored to this light. We read in this passage that the Bible reveals true life, it renews our vision, it restores others to this light. My prayer for you, Faith Bible Church. Is that God's word would sustain you in the season of life? Let me pray. Father, we thank you that though the darkness seems grim, you alone are the true light of this world. We thank you that you have placed that light within us. We pray for those of us whose light is flickering, feeling faint, feeling small Lord, maybe that's all of us in this room. We feel like we are hidden or placed under a basket, or we feel like our light is dying out. Lord, you are the one who suspends. You are the one who places us where we need to be. And so would you remind us of that truth today, tomorrow, during this week? Weak, give us faith to believe that you will sustain us. In Jesus' name, amen.

sermons.title: The Pharisaical Pharisees
sermons.speaker: Sung Cho
sermons.text: What is a Pharisee? Here's what we know. While some Pharisees were priests, most were not. Unlike Sadducees, who were urban elites in Jerusalem, Pharisees lived in the villages and cities of Israel. There they were respected and influential in religious communities. They emphasize the law of Moses and regard it as binding the ancestral interpretive traditions. Because of these traditions, a normal everyday Jew can faithfully interpret and embody the Torah, such as the law of purity and Sabbath restrictions. One practical application was the heightened emphasis on the table and table fellowship. What you eat and with whom you eat. If we were Jews living in first century Israel, we'd likely look off the Pharisees just as we do today with Christian leaders. But it doesn't take long in your New Testament reading plan to realize that Pharisees are often at odds with Jesus. Among all the groups that came in contact with Christ, they're the last group you want to be part of, right? Well, it does seem like you can be a Pharisee and a faithful Christian. Look at Nicodemus. He first came to Jesus by night, but later buried his body by day. basically declaring his faith in him by the time we get to John chapter 19. Consider how in Acts 15, at the Jerusalem Council, there were some of the sect of the Pharisees who believed. Now they need some correction, but they're believers nonetheless. Observe how throughout Acts, Paul is using his Pharisee credentials To preach Christ and synagogues throughout the Roman Empire. Note carefully how Paul can exclaim at his trial Men and brethren, I am a Pharisee, the son of a Pharisee, concerning the hope and resurrection of the dead, I am being judged. That's in Acts 23. Think of the benefits from Paul at Christ preaching Pharisee, whom we imitate as he imitated Christ. So, of course there's caveats. As long as you lay aside the tradition of men and hold the word of God As long as you count the title of Pharisee as lost for Christ, you can be a Pharisee and a faithful Christian. As long as you renounce self-righteousness for righteousness through faith, as long as you reckon yourself chief sinner before chief teacher. You can be a Pharisee and a faithful Christian. But even so, you must not be Pharisaical In other words, Paul was a Pharisee Christian, but he could not be a Pharisaical Pharisee Christian. Pharisee does not simply mean being a Pharisee, at least not today. Sometimes words like this one get detached from its origins. Merriam-Webster defines Fair Seiko like this, marked by hypocritical, censorious self-righteousness. Marked by hypocritical, censorious, self-righteousness But how do we know we're being very stable? One pastor named Terry Newark wrote a blog post discussing top tens Top 10 things bear cycle churchgoers say. Let me share a few. Perhaps you've heard some of these from others or out of your own mouth Maybe um you thought of these things in your heart. Here we go If he knew the Bible as well as I did, his life would be better. Here's another. Sure, I have a few issues, but that's between me and God. Let me share one more. People who don't go to church can come if they want to. I think this kind of discussion is helpful for application. But to get to the root of Pharisaical attitudes and actions, we need to dig into the word. What exactly made Pharisees, the enemies of Jesus and the early church, Pharisaical? Why did Jesus warn us to beware of their leaven? How do we identify their tendencies in us and ferret it out? We'll see it today in today's passage, Luke 11, 37 to 44. So let's read it together. Luke 11, 37 to 44. And as he spoke, a certain Pharisee asked him to dine with him. So he went in and sat down to eat. When the Pharisee saw it, he marveled that he had not first washed before dinner. Then the Lord said to him Now you Pharisees make the outside of the cup and dish clean, but your inward part is full of greed and wickedness. Foolish ones, did not he who made the outside make the inside also But rather give alms of such things as you have, then indeed all things are clean to you. But woe to you, Pharisees For you tithe, mint, and rule and all manner of herbs, and pass by justice and the love of God. These you ought to have done without leaving the others undone Woe to you, Pharisees, for you love the best seats in the synagogues and greetings in the marketplaces. Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! For you are like graves which are not seen, and the men who walk over them are not aware of them. So last week, Brother Alex preached on verses 33 to 36 concerning the light within us and the lamp that must shine for others. Like that previous passage, we can trace the movement from inward to outward, from private to public life, from ourselves to others Unlike that previous passage, we move through this one in a linear trajectory, verses 37, 38, 39, etc. Not in a sandwich structure. So here are four principles to avoid a Pharisaic path. One, prioritize inward purity and motives. That's verses 31, I'm sorry, 37 to 41. 2. Major on justice and love, verses 42. 3. Display humility before others, verse 43. And four, influence others toward godliness. Verse 44. First, prioritize inward purity and motives. Recall how Jesus warned us back in verse 35: Take heed that the light which is in you is not darkness. If you do not take heed, you'll get what you see in verses 37 to 41. The episode started out innocently enough. An unnamed Pharisee invited Jesus to dine with him. This isn't the first time a meal like this took place. Back in chapter 7, a Pharisee named Simon opened up his home to Jesus. But just as it happened at Simon's home, there would be a controversy followed by a lesson. In verse 38, the host was offended that Jesus did not follow protocol. Our Lord completely ignored proper decorum. The Pharisees valued so much. Just to be clear, these religious leaders are not worried about germs or social contact. They're concerned about ritual purity. Mark is helpful in explaining these customs in chapter 7, verses 3 to 4. May want to look it up later. Mark 7, 3 to 4. The Pharisees and all the Jews do not eat unless they wash their hands in a special way, holding the tradition of the elders. When they come from the marketplace, they do not eat unless they wash, and there are many other things which they have received and hold, like the washing of cups, pitchers, copper vessels, and pouches. Jesus knew well the reaction and the scandal that would follow. Imagine an American and he flies to South Korea, gets invited at a home. And purposefully ignores the protocol to take off the shoes. That's just a small tiny fraction, a mere taste of the grave insult the Pharisee felt. Yet Jesus did not apologize. He never broke the commands of God, but he did break the traditions of men. Jesus prioritized inward purity and motives above outward facade and actions. His response is skating. Talk about a party turning to a disaster. He called those wise in the eyes of the world foolish. He exposed those who look outwardly holy as wicked. He condemned those who appear generous as greedy. The Pharisees make the outside of the cup and dish clean and pay little attention to the inward part. What right does Jesus have to make such accusations? He appeals to God the Creator in verse 40. Did not he who made the outside make the inside also? The answer is yes. It's not that the outward appearance is completely irrelevant. God created both: both the external and the internal. He is sovereign over both and he wants holistic consistency between the two. God created us inside and out, and God knows us inside and out. He's omniscient. He's not limited in perspective like us The Lord does not see as man sees. For man looks at the outward appearance, but the Lord looks at the heart. 1 Samuel 16, verse 7. There's no creature hidden from his sight, but all things are naked and open to the eyes of him to whom we must give account. Hebrews 413 God created us inside and out, and He knows us inside and out. That's why we must prioritize inward purity and motives. But what does it mean practically to prioritize inward purity and motives? First I want to talk to Maybe those who are not Christians. There's no cleansing solution for my stained and blotted soul. Like Pilate, you can wash your hands before the multitude, but it's no use. Like Lady Macbeth, you can bid your sins out, damn spot out, I say, but it's no use. What's going to empty me of the greed and wickedness that's in me? Well, we have a heart problem. The heart is deceitful above all things and desperately wicked. Who can know it? Jesus knows it and warns us. Out of the heart proceed evil thoughts, murders, adulteries, fornications, thefts, false witnesses, blasphemies. These are the things which defile a man, but to eat with unwashed hands does not defile a man. That's Matthew 15, 19 to 20. Thankfully, the same Bible that teaches us we're wicked provides the solution. The solution is the gospel, the good news of Jesus. We've been reading and singing about it this morning. You read along David's Prayer to God, his only hope of forgiveness. Blot out my transgression, wash me thoroughly from my iniquity, and cleanse me from my sin. You've heard the promises of pardon If we confess our sins, He is faithful and just to forgive us our sins and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness. You sang, just as I am And waiting not to rid my soul of one dark blot, to thee whose blood can cleanse each spot. O Lamb of God, I come, I come. Jesus paid it all. All to him I owe. Sin had left the crimson stain. He washed it white as snow He breaks the power of cancelled sin. He sets the prisoner free. His blood can make the foulest clean. His blood availed for me. The blood of Jesus can make the fallest clean, inside and out. If you've never asked God to cleanse you of your sin, please beware, you cannot enter heaven in your current condition. God is holy and pure and perfect. Heaven is his abode, and he has every right to keep the impure out of it. But out of his love, he sent his son Jesus to die for us on the cross, the perfect, spotless Lamb. Died in our place and shed his blood for imperfect, spotted sinners. He rose from the dead to prove that he has accomplished his mission. He ascended to heaven. And sits at the right hand of the Father, awaiting his return. Now he asks you to come and accept this gracious gift of salvation by faith. You cannot earn it, deserve it, be worthy of it. In faith alone, reach out like a poor leper and be cleansed. We must prioritize this inward purity before anything else in life. Now, what about believers who are already saved? Prioritizing this inward purity and modus means not only coming to Christ initially for salvation, but also walking with him continually by the Spirit. Even though we're no longer under condemnation and the penalty of sin, we presently struggle with sin until we're home with the Lord. We resist those very sins that once kept us from heaven. If the Spirit confirms that we're vessels of mercy, not wrath, Let us be clean vessels, sanctified and useful for the Master, prepared for every good work. Jesus commands in verse 41 a specific application for the Pharisees, once they're saved, they should give away the riches they afforded. In other words, once you've been emptied of internal greed and wickedness, empty those external things that tempt you to be greedy and wicked. Once we understand the value of inward purity, our perspective of what's most important changes. The Pharisees did not have such a perspective, and so Jesus berates them with three woes in verses 42 to 44. That leads us to the second way to avoid the parasitical path, major unjustice and love. We saw woes earlier in Luke, back in chapter six, immediately following blessings. You can bet woe is opposite in meaning. To be precise, woe is a Hebrew interjection and onomatopoeia. It actually sounds like, oh, not the sound we make when we realize something, but more like the sound we make when we face calamity, as when we say, oh no Many woes, or I should say, o's, will be heard in hell. When the unbelieving rich become poor, full become hungry, laughter turns into mourning and weeping. There will be eternal regret and suffering. These Pharisees could not see their predicament ahead of them Their short-sightedness and myopia were fatal. They couldn't see the forest for the trees, or in this case, they couldn't see God's justice and love for the mint, roux, and all manner of tiny herbs. Now, such detailed tiding and measurements are not bad in themselves. In fact, Jesus says, these you ought to have done justice and love without leaving the others undone, measuring and tiding. But first, they should have majored on justice and love. How did these Pharisees pass by justice and the love of God? We turn to Micah 6, 6 to 8. You can look it up later, I'll just read it for you. Micah 6, 6 to 8. With what shall I come before the Lord and bow myself before the high God? Shall I come before him with burnt offerings, with calves, a year old? Will the Lord be pleased with thousands of rams, ten thousand rivers of oil? Shall I give my firstborn for my transgression, the fruit of my body, for the sin of my soul? He has shown you, O man, what is good. And what does the Lord require of you, but to do justly, to love mercy, and to walk humbly with your God? For the Pharisees, it was easier to measure out ten percent than give themselves hundred percent to God. These religious leaders major the minor issues and minor the major issues. Have you ever fallen into this trap? Perhaps you're so focused on money down to the last penny that you've neglected to defend a poor brother in Christ who's been denied justice in this society. Perhaps you're so focused on time down to the last minute that you've forgotten to give attention to the lonely widow. It's good to budget our resources of money and time, no doubt, but are you just as meticulous, demanding, and intense when it comes to justice and the love of God? Do you major on justice and love? No doubt all of us fail from time to time to major on the majors. And when we fail, we return to the gospel of Jesus every time. We see how for the sake of justice and love Jesus gave it all and died on the cross. He humbly took the place of shame to make us sit together in the heavenly places. That leads to the third way to avoid being pharisaical. Display humility before others. Adopting God's point of view leads us to a sober view of ourselves. Consider the seats of honor. We ought to be uncomfortable if people exalt us to the highest seats. We should take the lowest place and humble ourselves. Or consider the greetings in public places. Do not be like Haman, filled with wrath and Mordecai, who did not bow or pay him homage. Esther three, right? Instead, be sons of our heavenly Father and greet even your enemies, just not just your brethren. Matthew five, as Jesus told us. Display humility before others. Now the Bible is filled with practical principles and examples of humility But if you want to find the perfect model, look no further than our Lord Jesus Himself. Observe and study his life as recorded in the Gospels this coming week. In addition, we as church would love to come alongside you to read and study one of the four gospels with you. If you're interested, please speak to me after service. Leave a message online or drop a note in the offering box. There's none like Jesus to teach you humility. Let this mind be in you, which was also in Christ Jesus. I also want to directly encourage the leaders to display humility: elders, deacons, and teachers at church, patriarchs and matriarchs at home, managers and executives at work. In what ways have you guarded yourselves from pride? Beware the tendency to love the best seats in the synagogues and greetings in the marketplaces? It's in all of us. In my personal battle against vanity and honorable appearances, I'm taking an indefinite break from Facebook and Twitter. This may not seem like a big deal to you guys. But to be clear, this is not an application for everyone, right? But it is good for me. I'll be less tempted to exalt myself over others. And as an additional benefit, I'll be less tempted to despair and compare myself to people who look better than me. Another practical action is to display humility by using our recognized seats to exalt others. Let's consider one place of authority right here on the stage. Some people can some pastors can be possessive with the pulpit and never share it We should be happy to see younger, aspiring pastors develop their ministry skills here. As for teachers and leaders, Perhaps you can put the spotlight on the gifted but less recognized brothers or sisters, have them lead some of your classes In whatever way you practically apply this principle, leaders, display humility before others. We occupy influential seats. It's humbling to know that we shall receive stricter judgment. It's sobering because not only do we speak the word of God The example of our faith is followed, and the outcome of our conduct is considered. That leads to the next principle to avoid being parasitical: influence others toward godliness. When it comes to Christ's condemnation of evil leaders, there's always space for more. Jesus expands that woeful party to include Scribes. Scribes were most likely a special subset of Pharisees and also known as teachers of the law. If you look at Luke 5, that seems to be the case What's perfectly clear is that Jesus designates them together as hypocrites. Our Lord has more to say to them later with a more extended tirade in Matthew 23 at Jerusalem. In the second half of verse 44, Jesus exposes the spiritual deadness of these leaders. Numbers nineteen lists among the unclean, those who touched a grave. Unmarked graves were especially hazardous, threats to ritual purity. like hidden landmines. It's radical to think that Pharisees of all people will be condemned like this But the very fact that ordinary men look up to them as examples of holiness makes them extraordinarily dangerous. They did not influence others toward godliness. Saints do not be charmed by a leader merely in his or her word. Observe if there's godly conduct, love, spirit, faith, purity Stay clear of teachers that merely hear the word on Sunday and never do it. Avoid mere talkers, those who read God's word like a mirror, but forget what they beheld a minute they walk away. Watch out for pastors who build houses on sand instead of building it on a rock. The rain will descend. The floods will come, and the winds will blow and beat on those houses. Their fall will be great Many leaders do not influence others toward godliness. I pray our church is filled with good leaders, godly leaders. I pray that our membership is full of individuals who influence others toward godliness. As an application, passages like this one can guide us if we're looking for a congregation to join, whether it's here at Faith Bible Church or elsewhere. Carefully read over the church's statement of faith, listen to their sermons, look up the pastor's Bile, educational background, and ministry training, but wait, you're not done. Actually, go and attend the church for a few weeks or even a few months. While there, observe the pastors, along with the elders, the deacons. And the staff members. See if the fancy website, the polite emails, and the quality sermon recordings have true substance behind them. Pay attention to the way they talk to their spouses and children, their attitudes toward outsiders, other local pastors and churches. Do they lead a healthy church that will edify and promote your growth? Or are they unmarked graves that will contaminate your spiritual life unawares? Do they influence others toward godliness? Now, how about you personally? Are you influencing others toward godliness? You don't need to occupy a formal position of authority to be Pharisaical. Whether your sphere of influence is great or small, God sees all that you do inside and out. He also sees the great damage you cause with hypocrisy. We often fail to influence others toward godliness. But we find grace in Jesus. For those who are cleansed by the blood of the Lamb, be reminded of our hope of righteousness. It's not in our clean outward public image It's certainly not in our inconsistent private life. We fail, but we can get back up because of Christ at the right hand of God. Our perfect leader. Behold him there, the risen Lamb, my perfect spotless righteousness. The great, unchangeable I am, the king of glory and of grace. One with himself I cannot die. My soul is purchased by his blood. My life is hid with Christ on high, with Christ my Savior and my God. Let's pray. No, we come before you Yielding, surrendering, knowing that there's no hiding from you. And that has always been the case. Lord, we're thankful for this many of us here who do know you. Lord, that you accept us with all our faults. And Lord, you gave us forgiveness through your Son Jesus Christ. But Lord, remind us once again. of your just anger against hypocrisy, leadership that does not influence toward godliness Lord, ways that we forget that even after walking in the Lord for many years, that you care about what's going on inside of us. The coveting, the jealousy, the idolatries that we may harbor in our hearts, we confess them before you And we are reminded that nothing can cleanse us thoroughly, nothing can save us, nothing can help us grow spiritually. Except by the power of your word, your spirit. And we come before you. And every time we fail, we want to be reminded. Of the finished work of your Son Jesus Christ at the cross. We're thankful and help us this week. Help us each and every day. To have a consistent life, integrity, to confess before you the sins that we harbor in our hearts, and to live a life of holiness. We thank you and we pray all these things in Jesus Christ's name. Amen.

sermons.title: Woe to You Also Lawyers
sermons.speaker: Sung Cho
sermons.text: So the last church I belonged to was known for promoting the idea of nine marks as a nine marks of a healthy church. Based on that, the Presbyterian Kevin DeYoung wrote a TGC piece entitled Nine Marks of an Unhealthy Church. I want to share some of these with you, but we're not here to use these to be judgmental or bludgeon other churches. We should first take a close look at ourselves. We ought to guard ourselves from these traits vigilantly. I'll just share three. Here's one. The more peripheral the sermon topic, the more excited the people become. The more peripheral the sermon topic, the more excited the people become. In other words, the church cares very little about the major doctrines of inerrancy, trinity, salvation. They care most about classes of angels or something like how to feel good about yourself. Here's another The leadership team never changes or always changes. The leadership team never changes or always changes. Of course, there may be many reasons for this, but very often lack of biblical discipleship leads to lack of biblical leadership. Or members depart all the time, the pool of volunteers is running thin, or the staff of pastors never stick around. One more. There are issues everyone knows about, but no one talks about openly. There are issues everyone knows about, but no one talks about openly. Some are too polite or too scared to call out glaring problems that need to be addressed. I mean who wants to talk about accountability, evaluation, and church discipline? Right? I'm sure there are many ways a church can or church culture can become unhealthy In order to avoid an unhealthy church, we need to take a hard look at God's word. Are there traditions, attitudes, and instability that we need to check? Do we confront the issues that hinder us from growth? Can the woes of Jesus against the religious leaders and his generation teach us anything? Let's turn to Luke eleven, forty-five to fifty-four for answers. Then one of the lawyers answered and said to him, Teacher, by saying these things you reproach us also. And he said, Woe to you also, lawyers, for you loathe men with burdens hard to bear, and you yourselves do not touch the burdens with one of your fingers Woe to you, for you build the tombs of the prophets, and your fathers killed them. In fact, you bear witness that you approve the deeds of your fathers, for they indeed killed them, and you build their tombs. Therefore the wisdom of God also said, I will send them prophets and apostles, and some of them they will kill and persecute. That the blood of all the prophets, which was shed from the foundation of the world, may be required of this generation, from the blood of Abel to the blood of Zechariah, who perished between the altar and the temple. Yes, I say to you, it shall be required of this generation. Woe to you, lawyers, for you have taken away the key of knowledge You did not enter in yourselves, and those who were entering in you hindered. And as he said these things to them, the scribes and the Pharisees began to assail him vehemently and to cross examine him about many things, lying in wait for him, and seeking to catch him in something he might say, that they might accuse him Though much of the harsh rhetoric here do not apply to us directly I believe there are three principles to help us avoid an unhealthy church culture. One, unbiblical traditions load difficult burdens on others. That's verses 45 to 46. Two, unbelieving hostility opposes God's wisdom and messengers, verses forty-seven to fifty-one And three, unreliable leadership harms kingdom seekers. Verses 52 to 54 First, unbiblical traditions load difficult burdens on others. In verse 45, we're reintroduced to the lawyers. Now, lawyers in this context are not jurisdoctors of today, they're experts in the law of Moses. They're synonymous with scribes and probably the same as the teachers of the law. One way to look at lawyers is to see them as priests off duty. They served as legal ex experts when they weren't performing their temple duties. But all their expertise will not do them any good. We saw earlier in chapter seven, verse thirty, that they along with the Pharisees Rejected the will of God for themselves, not having been baptized by John the Baptist. They would also reject Jesus the Messiah, whom John proclaimed. In chapter 10, we saw one of them stand up to test Jesus, and he was humiliated when he tried to justify himself. Evidently, some of the lawyers were there at the Pharisees' home and near the table where this controversy was brewing. We saw the woes against the Pharisees last time. And they were triggered by them. It turns out that scribes, Pharisees, and now lawyers, they were united in their hate against Christ and united in their love of tradition. So now Jesus directs his attack on the lawyers. The first woe is in verse 46. Lawyers are held responsible for the burdens they put on others, burdens so difficult that even they couldn't carry them. What are these burdens? They're unbiblical oral traditions. They include the elaborate hand washing rituals in this context. In other places we learn of strict Sabbath restrictions that hinder the hungry, the poor, and the sick. These lawyers share the Pharisees' guilt. Like the Pharisees in verse 42, they passed by justice and the love of God. Like the Pharisees of Acts 15. They test God by putting a yoke on the neck no one could bear, not even their patriarchs. Like the Pharisees of Matthew 23, they bind heavy burdens. Hard to bear, and lay them on men's shoulders, but they themselves will not move them with one of their fingers The lawyers held to unbiblical traditions that loaded difficult burdens on others. What should they have done instead? Look at verse 46 again. The verb touch there evokes an image of warmth and kindness. which these law experts lacked. Commentator A. T. Robertson observes, quote, A physician would understand the meaning of the word touch here for feeling gently a sore spot or a pulse. Well these lawyers had no pulse on their patients. They were sole physicians with poor bedside manners. They lacked a healing touch to address the sore spot. They used unbiblical tradition to load difficult burdens on others. Contrast that with the loving touch of Jesus. See his healing hand extending to the leper. Peter's sick mother-in-law. Jairus' daughter, the demoniac's son, the blind man, the Malchus' ear Hear his patient care for the lost. Those who are well have no need of a physician, but those who are sick. I have not come to call the righteous but sinners to repentance. Accept his loving invitation. Matthew 11, 28 to 30. Come to me, all you who labor and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest. Take my yoke upon you and learn from me, for I am gentle and lowly in heart, and you will find rest for your souls. For my yoke is easy, and my burden is light. While unbiblical tradition loads difficult burdens on others, Jesus came to unload those burdens. More on more on exact details of how later, but for now I want to ask ourselves How do we make sure difficult, burdensome, and unbiblical traditions do not seep into our church? How do we make sure that God's word reigns supreme? How do we make sure traditions we hold to are regularly evaluated? We have multiple safeguards in place, but I would say that among the most important safeguards is a specific sermon style. It's called expository preaching. My former pastor defines expository preaching as that type of preaching in which the points of the sermon are the points of the text. Again, the points of the sermon are the points of the text. This is good because we don't want the points of the sermon to be my opinions, my agenda, my pet peeps. or whatever I saw on the news recently. We don't want the points of the sermon to be based on some cherished unbiblical tradition. Expository preaching is an important way to avoid loading difficult burdens on others. Now, from the perspective of the member or church attender, how can you make sure no one puts unbiblical burdens on your shoulders? The application is similar. When you feel pressure from a leader, teacher, or an elder, first check to see whether this is truly a burden from the Lord. Consider how the ancient prophets were faithful in delivering God's message, and note how that message is often called a burden. Isaiah, Ezekiel, Nahum, Habakkuk, Zachariah, and Malachi all speak of their message as burdens from the Lord. See if the weight they put on you is according to the Bible. Be like the fair-minded Bharaans and search the scriptures daily. Such is the way to break the yoke that is on biblical tradition. Such is the means to maturity Such is the principle for wise living. Speaking of wise living, let's turn now to the second principle Unbelieving hostility opposes God's wisdom and messengers The next woe begins in verse forty-seven. We switch from the imagery of burdens to tombs that house venerable men. But it might be most helpful to focus not on a location, but time, specifically past, present, and future. Past with regard to the Old Testament prophets and forefathers. Present with regard to Jesus and the religious leaders in the Gospels. And future with regard to the early church and their persecutors in Acts and beyond. The principle that ties past, present, and future together is this. leaving hostility. Let's start with the past and the present together Imagine the shock of these lawyers who venerate the prophets, but are now told they practically bury them themselves. Jesus takes complicity to a whole new level. We're not talking just a few years, decades, or centuries. We're talking about thousands of years of martyrdom pinned on this generation that rejected Jesus. Joseph Fitzmeier summarizes it well, quote, Unless this generation breaks with the past, it will answer for all the injustice done from the first to the last person. murdered in the first and last books of the Hebrew canon of the Old Testament. That's Abel in Genesis. To Zechariah in 2 Chronicles. The Hebrew order of the Old Testament, as we call it, ends with 2 Chronicles. That's why Zechariah is at the tail end of that. Now, these religious leaders might object. If we had lived in the days of our fathers, we would not have been partakers with them in the blood of the prophets. Yet their treatment of Jesus suggests otherwise. Their hostility against Christ proves that they're no better than their forefathers. They're actually far worse. They deserve a worse punishment than their fathers because at least the older ones, they didn't actually see the Messiah in front of them. Their ancestors may have attacked the messengers and the ambassadors, but these lawyers went after the Messiah and the king. So if we learn, so we learn that if they attack the substance in Christ, they also attack the shadows. If they disobey God, who has in these last days spoken to us by his son, they disobey the same God who spoke in time past to the fathers by the prophets. By rejecting Jesus, they also rejected all things written in the law of Moses and the prophets and the Psalms concerning Jesus. Have they in fact rejected Jesus? Yes, and here's the evidence. Observe the religious leaders' unbelieving hostility throughout the Gospels. Jesus has shown them many good works from the Father, but they refuse to believe. Some try to throw him off the cliff or stone him. They not only laid aside God's word in books, they've opposed God's word in flesh. This evil generation revile the one greater than Jonah, the one greater than Solomon. Also look at the unbelieving hostility at the end of the Gospels. We know how all four of them end. These rulers reject God's wisdom. They're about to crucify the Lord of glory. These leaders reasoned among themselves, saying, This is the heir. Come, let us kill him that the inheritance may be offered. They unjustly shed the blood of God's Son, through whom the worlds were made. So now the blood of all the prophets shed from the foundation of the world justly falls on them So what connects the past with the present is the one and the same unbelieving hostility. But not only are these lawyers guilty of rejecting the martyrs of the past and Jesus in their present, they'll be guilty of rejecting him and his followers in the future. Look at the prophecy of verse 49. The mention of wisdom of God there is interesting. Wisdom of God is a title for Jesus, like Word of God or Lamb of God. Matthew chapter 23, verse 34 confirms this. The wisdom of God here corresponds to I, that is Jesus, there. Right? Again, Matthew 23, 34. Jesus is the wisdom of God. This is confirmed elsewhere in the scriptures. Jesus' divine wisdom personified even more so than Lady Wisdom in Proverbs 9, which we read earlier. Paul says, In Christ are hidden all the treasures of wisdom and knowledge. To those called to believe, both Jews and Greeks, Christ is the power of God and the wisdom of God. After his ascension to heaven, Jesus sends his own prophets, wise men, and scribes These are the earliest Christians who continue their ministry among the Jews. They too will face unbelieving hostility. Jesus specifies in Matthew 23, which happens a little bit later in Jerusalem, some of them you will kill and crucify. Some of them you will scourge in your synagogues and persecute from city to city. That's what awaited the early church in Acts and beyond So what connects the future with the past and the present is the one and the same unbelieving hostility that opposes God's wisdom. How does this principle relate to us? Today, unbelieving hostility may not come from Israelite leaders But it continues nonetheless. Other institutions, rulers, and authorities oppose those sent by Jesus. We, along with the persecuted church, fill up in our flesh what is lacking in the afflictions of Christ. In other words, the world's not done persecuting Jesus yet, and we're the means to do just that. So what is the proper response to this unbelieving hostility? It should be faith. Our prayer each day should be increase our faith. The best defense against hostile unbelief is our patient belief. Fight the good fight of faith. Stand fast in one spirit, with one mind striving together for the faith of the gospel, and not in any way terrified by your adversaries. Trust in God's sovereign plan. The same wisdom of God who sent prophets and apostles into the line of fire says to you Go and make disciples of all the nations. We live by faith. We advance. We do not draw back. All who desire to live godly in Christ Jesus will suffer persecution. Look to the prize when our faith is sight. We must through many tribulations enter the kingdom of God. To be really specific in our time and location, American evangelicals may be facing some tough times ahead One lawyer and professor, Kenneth Craycraft, believes religious conservatives should prepare themselves for battle on three ethical fronts. Abortion, gender ideology, and religious liberty. He concludes his thoughts with this warning Quote, of course, no politician, law, regulation, or policy can take away one's religious faith, but they can make it very costly to practice one's faith. And they can impose moral positions on people of faith that force them either to participate in falsehood or face severe financial and even legal sanctions. But even if we face unbelieving hostility in the days to come, let's respond in faith. Like we sang earlier, let's not fear, for this truth remains, that our God is the ancient of days. Now you see how grave the consequences are when leaders adhere to unbiblical traditions and harbor unbelieving hostility. And that leads to the next principle, unreliable leadership harms kingdom seekers We saw in verse 44 that the hypocrisy of Pharisees and scribes makes them unmarked graves that defile their followers. Verse 52 communicates a similar idea here. These lawyers do not influence others toward godliness. Quite the opposite. See, their job is to faithfully transmit the scriptures to the people. These leaders should have taught themselves God's word and then share what they've learned. See how important this task is considering the situation in the first century. Literacy rate was quite low by modern standards Most Jews could not go to a bookstore and purchase personal copies of their study Bible, right? They couldn't sign up and participate in annual Bible reading plans on their smartphones. They couldn't go online and listen to preachers on YouTube in the evening with bright lamps lit. These laymen depended heavily on the clergy. More than we can imagine today. But since these leaders were so fixated on teachings of men, they did not disseminate the teachings of God. See Marvin Pate comments, quote, the idea is that scries incrustation of the Word of God, like that word incrustation. of the Word of God with the traditions of men keep people from encountering the revelation of God. End quote Can you picture thick layers of crust that keeps us from the precious Word of God? That's what they use to hinder others. Unreliable leadership harms kingdom seekers. Jesus exposed their evil agenda and their response is predictably hostile. They will not listen to the rebuke, correction, and instruction of divine wisdom. The reaction in verses 53 and 54 is foretold in ancient Proverbs: A scoffer does not listen to rebuke, does not love one who corrects him. He who hates correction is stupid. He who disdains instruction despises his own soul. Instead of taking Christ's yoke and learning from him, they start to set traps for him, to take him down. Instead of finding rest for their souls, they're restless in finding ways to ruin him. This kind of leadership is not only directly harmful, it's also indirectly destructive through widespread influence. That's what leadership is about, right? Influence. And this was an evil prototype for others to follow Later, when there was a chance that Jesus might be uh released by Pilate, what did the ungodly leaders do? The chief priests and the elders persuaded the multitudes that they should ask for Barabas and destroy him. Jesus. When it was clearly evident that Jesus rose from the dead, what did they do? They bribed the soldiers who guarded the tomb and spread the lie that his disciples came at night and stole him away while they slept. When Stephen, the follower of Jesus, spoke with irresistible wisdom and spirit, what did they do? They stirred up the people, the elders, and the scribes, and they came upon him. seized them and brought them to the council. When revival took place in Iconium under Paul and Barnabas, what did they do? The unbelieving Jews stirred up the Gentiles and poisoned their minds against the brethren. See how unreliable leadership harms kingdom seekers. They perpetuate unbiblical traditions and inculcate. Unbelieving hostility. But again, we must remember that at times we display the same devotion to unbiblical traditions. The same unbelieving hostility, and the same unreliable leadership. We have the root of the lawyer's evil, even if we don't always display the fruit. Well, what's the solution? It's the gospel. To save us from the woes that we deserve, God the Father sent His Son, Jesus, to earth. As God and man at the same time, He lived a perfect life. Whereas the lawyers reject the commandments of God to keep the tradition, Jesus, whom God sent speaks the words of God and fulfills the law and the prophets. Whereas the lawyers displayed unbelieving hostility towards God's wisdom, Jesus was filled with wisdom, grew in it, and shared it with others. Whereas the lawyers exemplify unreliable leadership concerning knowledge, Jesus openly preached the gospel and offered the truth that would make them free. Jesus lived as a perfect leader. Then Jesus died as the perfect servant leader. Unlike the lawyers who do not touch others' burdens, Jesus carried upon his shoulders the burden of our sins, the iniquity of us all. And climbed Calvary. He climbed he climbed there and he died on the cross for our sins. Paying the penalty for of our sins, of eternal condemnation on our behalf, so that you can live with them forever. He rose from the dead as proof of this transaction, completed and ascended to heaven. Someday he'll return to exact revenge against those who opposed his wisdom and messengers. Until then, this key of knowledge is offered to you. Jesus will not hinder you from entering the kingdom. Jesus is the door of the sheep, the way, the truth, and the life. No one comes to the Father except through Him. He welcomes all who are wary and oppressed under unbiblical traditions and leadership. If you haven't already done so, come to him. Turn away from your unbelief and hostility. Trust in Christ for your hope of eternal life. You cannot earn salvation or deserve it. You receive it as a gift of grace by faith. Wherever you are, whether you're at an unhealthy church or a healthy one. Whether you're in a bad relationship or a good relationship, whether you're in the pits or in the heights, we should come to Him. For the Lord is good and faithful. He will keep us day and night. We can always run to Jesus. Jesus strong and Let's pray. Lord, we come before you, and some of us may just be tired of the burdens that are put on us. Each day is just survival, a desperate attempt at survival. But we feel the burdens from our responsibilities. We feel the burdens of parenting. Of being good spouses, being good workers. We're thankful that we can come to you to find rest. That we can be just your children who cry out our Father before you That we don't have to impress you, we don't have to come to you with all the things that we have accomplished as a list. We don't have to be like the first son in the prodigal son parable. That you accept us in your gracious love for us. Or even in this passage that warns against the opposite, help us or to take heed lest we hold to umbilical traditions. Thest we have hostility in our hearts, lest we follow leaders that are unreliable. But we're thankful that you are always reliable. That we can look to you. And we can look to men and women who follow the example of your Son. And we also look to ourselves. Make us more like your Son Jesus Christ. Each and everyone. Every day. Pray all these things in Jesus Christ's name. Amen. E

sermons.title: Our Faith, Inside and Out
sermons.speaker: Sung Cho
sermons.text: The unseen affects the seen, the invisible, the visible, the private, the public Two illustrations. First, the great Michelangelo painted the ceiling of the Sistine Chapel, lying on his back for hours, to finish every detail with great care. It is said a friend asked why he took such pains with figures that would be viewed from such a considerable distance. After all, who will notice whether it's perfect or not? I will, replied the artist. Second, Birch Khalifa in Dubai stands as the world's tallest building Over a half a mile tall with 160 floors. A building this massive can only stand because workers spent a year digging and pouring the foundation. And a foundation that contains 58,000 cubic yards of concrete weighing more than 110 tons Great public artwork and edifices must be designed masterfully, inside and out. In the parts seen and unseen, visible and invisible The same holds truth with our faith, with this private and public dimensions As we continue in Luke, we'll find principles to be strong and firm in our faith, inside and out. So let's read Luke twelve, one to twelve, together. Luke twelve, one to twelve In the meantime, when an innumerable multitude of people had gathered together, so that they trampled one another, he began to say to his disciples, first of all, Beware of the leaven of the Pharisees, which is hypocrisy. For there is nothing covered that will not be revealed, nor hidden that will not be known. Therefore, whatever you have spoken in the dark will be heard in the light And what you have spoken in the ear in inner rooms will be proclaimed on the housetops. And I say to you, my friends, do not be afraid of those who kill the body, and after that have no more that they can do. But I will show you whom you should fear. Fear him who after he has killed has power to cast into hell. Yes, I say to you, fear him. Are not five sparrows sold for two copper coins, and not one of them is forgotten before God But the very hairs of your head are all numbered. Do not fear, therefore, you are of more value than many sparrows Also, I say to you, whoever confesses me before men, him, the Son of Man, also will confess before the angels of God. But he who denies me before men will be denied before the angels of God. And anyone who speaks a word against the Son of Man, it will be forgiven him. But to him who blasphemes against the Holy Spirit, it will not be forgiven. Now when they bring you to the synagogues and magistrates and authorities, do not worry about how or what you should answer or what you should say. For the Holy Spirit will teach you in that very hour what you ought to say. How do we strengthen our faith inside and out? One, beware of hypocrisy that God judges, verses one to three. 2. Fear the Almighty, loving God, verses 4 to 7. And 3, trust in the Spirit to witness for Christ, verses 8 to 12. First, beware of hypocrisy that God judges. So not too long after Jesus left the house, the home of the Pharisee. An innumerable multitude of people had gathered together. There were so many that they trampled one another It will be easy for anyone to get carried away by vast numbers, but Jesus is wise. Even if many professed to believe in his name because of the signs, he did not commit himself to them because he knew all men. And what exactly was in a man? Hypocrisy. Man may not see hypocrisy, but God sees it clearly. What is hypocrisy? The word has its roots in the world of Greek playwrights and performing arts. A hypocrite was a masked actor or stage player, literally meaning interpreter from underneath. That is, the character puts on a mask and from underneath the mask interprets the story through acting. By extension, hypocrisy can be a negative trait. In Greek translations of the Old Testament, we see the word hypocrisy used to translate the Hebrew word for ungodliness. Closer to our time, Miriam Webster defines it as a feigning to be what one is not, or to believe what one does not. Behavior that contradicts what one claims to believe or feel, especially the false assumption of an appearance of virtue or religion. The famed philosopher the Duke of Rouchefoucault once observed, quote, hypocrisy is a tribute that vice pays to virtue. Ultimately, we don't need French aphorisms or Greek word studies to grasp hypocrisy. It's one of those words that you understand from your gut. You know it when you see it. We don't need extensive training to be hypocrites either. It's easily caught even if it's not taught. And when leaders lead the way of hypocrisy, it spreads like yeast in a dough. That's the familiar image Jesus uses in verse 1. Yeast, once mixed in, is not something that's easily extracted, and that's the point. Anyone who bakes knows that that's how yeast makes the bread rise properly. In the same way, the woeful Pharisees Along with their scribes, taught hypocrisy thoroughly and pervasively among the masses. Beware of the hypocrisy that God judges. And how will God judge hypocrisy? Jesus warns us of the judgment to come in verses two and three. All cover-ups, every conspiracy, every hidden agenda will be revealed and no. It's not because our detectives or our justice system is perfect. It's not because we're prescient. It's because God is omniscient. There is no creature hidden from his sight. But all things are naked and open to the eyes of Him to whom we must give account. In that day of judgment, God reveals all, knows all, hears all, and proclaims all. There's no escape from him. God created you inside and out and knows you inside and out. You face a judge that has all the facts before him, whether it's unseen or the seen, the invisible or the visible, the private or the public, it makes no difference. He sees them all as clear as day. We can flee from the wrath to come, but there's no earthly refuge to enter. We can cry out to the mountains and rocks, fall on us and hide us from the face of him who sits on the throne and from the wrath of the land. But behold, the day is coming. Burning like an oven. And all the proud, yes, all who do wickedly will be stubborn. And the day which is coming shall burn them up, says the Lord of hosts. Is there no rescue from God's wrath? There is. Here's the good news Since there is no hiding from him, our only hope is that somehow, some way, we need to make sure all of our recorded sins are not counted against us. Is that even possible? Listen carefully to Paul's words in Romans 4, 5-8. To him who does not work, but believes on him, who justifies the ungodly. His faith is accounted for, righteousness, just as David also describes the blessedness of the man to whom God imputes righteousness, apart from works. Blessed are those whose lawless deeds are forgiven and whose sins are covered. Blessed is the man to whom the Lord shall not impute sin. We could savor on these promises for hours. Paul notes how King David, a very imperfect and immoral man with his own dirty laundry list. Of cover-ups, secret sins, and scandals, agendas, and conspiracies, came to find pardon, covering an erasure of his stained record. In David's record, there is now nothing covered to be revealed, nothing hidden to be known. Before God, there is nothing spoken in the dark to be heard in the light. There's nothing spoken in the ear in inner rooms to be proclaimed on the housetops. How did this happen? It's not because David made up for his mistakes by trying harder, becoming a better person, or outweighing his bad works with good ones. He was saved because he had faith in God. He trusted in the promises of a savior to come. His descendant, yet his Lord, the one we know as Jesus Christ. We know in much more detail than David what Jesus did for us. He's God's son, and he lived a perfect life. Committed no sin, nor was deceit found in his mouth. Yet he faced a criminal's execution on the cross. He was crucified as our substitute. Dying in our place for our sins. This was the Father's will. He made him who knew no sin. to be sin for us, that we might become the righteousness of God in him Now, all our moral failures, all our record, the handwriting of requirements that was against us, which was contrary to us, Jesus took them all and bled to wipe them off our books. Then Jesus rose from the dead as proof of this accomplishment and ascended to heaven. Someday he'll return to judge the living and the dead. Are you ready to have your books opened at the tribunal that day? Do you want assurance that God won't judge you based on your sins? You can come to Jesus now to the same faith that saved Abraham, David, and Paul. Turn away from your sins and turn to Christ. Trust in Him alone for eternal life and cleansing. You cannot earn it or deserve it. You accept salvation as a gift of grace, not by works. You can have this blessed confidence and assurance. Therefore, there is now no condemnation to those who are in Christ Jesus. If God is for us, who can be against us? With God as your advocate, what is there to fear anymore? That leads to the next principle for firm faith. Fear the Almighty loving God. Something being fearless is what we need to live out our faith. Yet Jesus teaches not the absence of fear, but fearing the right thing, or more accurately, the right being. That being none other than God Himself, if we fear God more, we fear men less. If we truly understood God's might and mercy We live in victory and confidence. We must have a spirit to fear God, to revere his power and love. Then we won't have a spirit of fear of man, but of power and of love and of a sound mind Jesus gently leads into this discussion of fear by addressing his disciples as friends. In no way does being Jesus' friend conflict with being his disciple. Being Jesus' friend means doing whatever he commands you. Christ has authority and he chose you and appointed you that you should go and bear fruit. And that your fruit should remain. But being friends with God's Son is not easy. To be a friend of God means enmity with the world. And this world is hostile to us. As Jesus warns later, if you were of the world, the world would love its own. Yet because you are not of the world, but I chose you out of the world, therefore the world hates you. As Martin Luther observed, and we sang earlier, this world with devils filled threatened to undo us. But our Lord also teaches us the limitations of the world in verse 4. Its inhabitants may threaten to undo us, but after they kill the body. There's no more that they can do. Then Jesus teaches us the non-limitations of God in verse 5. Jesus was even more explicit earlier in Matthew 10, 28. Do not fear those who kill the body but cannot kill the soul, but rather fear him who is able to destroy both soul and body in hell. Those who have the world as their enemy, death is the end of their troubles. Those who have God as their enemy, that is only the beginning of their troubles. The enemy of the world may have the power of first death to cast into dark graves, but these graves will be emptied one day God, on the other hand, has the power of second death to cast into the fiery lake. This lake will be filled forever. Fear the Almighty God This fear is such a point of emphasis that you see the verb fear three times in one verse, verse five, yet in the same breath. Jesus transitions seamlessly to the comforting words of verse 6. We learn that not only is God Almighty, He's also loving. Not only do we consider the severity of God, we consider the goodness of God. In these verses, we apply what we sang earlier. Ponder anew what the Almighty can do if with his love he befriend thee. God's not only Almighty, He's also loving. The one who reveals all, knows all, hears all, proclaims all, also values all. The argument proceeds from the lesser to the greater. Our Father knows every insignificant creature that has ever lived. He does not forget them. None of them passed without his knowledge. The sparrows were as insignificant as you can get, a cheap source of food. Jesus spoke of these birds earlier in Matthew 10, 29. How you could get two for one copper coin, which was about a tenth of the daily wage at that time. Interestingly, here you get five for two coins. The seller is basically saying, buy four for two coins, and I'll throw in an extra one for free Not highly esteemed before men, but not forgotten before God either God's intimate knowledge also extends to the very hairs on our heads. An average person has about 100,000 follicles there. He knows every one of these as well. If we have confidence that God cares for the sparrows How much more should we have confidence that God cares for the saints? You are of more value than many sparrows. How much value? Remember, you're bought at a price. As we sang earlier, and he will hold me fast. Those he saves are his delight. Christ will hold me fast. Precious in his holy sight. He will hold me fast. He'll not let my soul be lost. His promises shall last. Bought by him at such a cost. He will hold me fast. The same hand of God Almighty that throws the unsaved into hell lovingly holds us out of eternal danger. No one is able to snatch us out of his hand. So then the fear that's commanded in these verses isn't a paralyzing terror of a stormy despot, a capricious tyrant, or an unstable ruler. God's not someone with whom you feel like you're walking on eggshells. He's our loving Father. And yet He deserves our godly fear. This healthy reverence of God the Father helps us to witness for God the Son. And we'll also need the power of God the Spirit And that leads us to our third principle to strengthen our faith. Trust in the Spirit to witness for Christ. Every verse from verse eight to twelve Jesus refers to some kind of speech act. In verse 8, confess. In verse 9, deny. In verse 10, speak a word and blaspheme. In verse 11, answer and say, and in verse 12, teach and say. God never intended for our faith to be mute It's necessary for us to speak for him, just as it was necessary for Christ to suffer and to rise from the dead the third day It's necessary that repentance and remission of sins should be preached in his name to all nations. The followers of Jesus were witnesses of these things. So then if these disciples should keep silent, the stones would cry out. We have in verses 8 and 9 two scenarios concerning our public witness. We must make a choice. In verse 8, there's a bold declaration of faith in Jesus as that faith is proved to be genuine. We might picture Stephen in Acts 7 Rejected in the earthly court, but accepted in the heavenly one. In verse 9, there's a cowardly denial of Jesus. Faith proved to be ingenuine We might picture Peter in Luke 22 denying Jesus three times. But it's important to remember that verse nine need not be the final verdict on us and our lives. Remember God's grace. Apostle Peter, who at the high priest's courtyard failed to make his confession, found mercy from Jesus, the apostle and high priest of our confession. Satan wanted to sift Peter like wheat, that is, take them apart. But Jesus had prayed for him that his faith should not fail, even after his denial. That's why even though Peter failed in his confession, he did not fail in his faith. The same grace is given to us. In other words, even if you've been more like Peter than Stephen, even if you failed like verse 9 before. You can find grace to fulfill verse 8. The second chance comes from an intimate, saving relationship with Christ that cannot be severed Thank God that our salvation is not based on our courage or lost because of our cowardice. Thank God our salvation is based on Jesus' finished work on the cross. He paid for all our sins, even the sin of denial. So if you've been like Peter, but you've been you're a true believer You may be denied rewards in heaven, but you won't be denied your place in heaven Okay, so you failed to confess Christ bold, but you confessed your failure. Since denial is not an unforgivable sin, you found mercy, and now you're ready to try again. As you go out into the world and live out your faith, the cry of your hearts may be, Lord, I believe. Help my unbelief. We'll be talking about getting that help in verses 11 and 12, but first we have to talk about verse 10 From verses 8 to 10, there almost seems to be a progression or digression from the best we can say for Jesus to the worst we can say against him. Verse 8, confess Jesus. Awesome. Verse 9, deny Jesus, not good. First half of verse 10, speak against Jesus. Really bad. Second half of verse 10, blaspheme the Holy Spirit working through Jesus. That's The worst thing you can do. Whereas denying and speaking against Jesus can be forgiven, blasphemy the Spirit won't be. What exactly is this blasphemy of the Holy Spirit? This is a difficult topic, so we start with what's crystal clear. I'll repeat what I said from our Wednesday night studies on doctrines: quote: The blasphemy against the Holy Spirit is an eternal sin. And can never be forgiven. That's what it says. By the very nature of the sin, it cannot be committed by the true believer who is permanently indwelt by God's Spirit. End quote. It seems to be a sin that's categorically uncommittable by a true believer. I don't think we can define it simply as unbelief or resistance. Because God has definitely forgiven people of death, and many of us are living proofs of it Based on Jesus' earlier warnings against the Pharisees and scribes, I gather that this blasphemy is attributing Jesus' miraculous works to demonic powers. I believe that this specific blasphemy cannot be committed when Jesus is absent from earth. Just as the sin of Judas Iscariot and Pilate are unique sins at a unique time in history, the blasphemy against the Spirit is a unique sin of that time. These unbelieving Jewish leaders who have access to the clear testimonies of God, Jesus Himself, the testimony of John the Baptist, the works of the Holy Spirit through Jesus, the scriptures and the words of Moses. Chose willingly to go a step further and attribute Jesus' works to Billzebub. They were bent on discrediting Jesus at all costs. And what a cost it was. And their hostility against Jesus will continue against his followers. As they bring them to the synagogues and magistrates and authorities. Now, just from verses 8, 9, 10, and the first half of verse 11, the disciples might be scared out of their wits. They're probably thinking, so Jesus, you're telling us that while we may confess you before men, we might also deny you out of fear. Will face not only people who speak against you, but also attribute your works to the devil. These enemies of God may drag us before the leading Jews of the day and embarrass us with difficult Bible questions. This sounds really tough. Nonetheless, against such immense pressure, Jesus basically says Akunamatara. You won't be tongue-tied, even if you're tied in bonds and chains. The Holy Spirit will teach you. The Holy Spirit is the difference between Peter at the end of the Gospels and Peter in the book of Acts, between the disciples who fled and the disciples who stayed. The disciples in the Gospels could not keep the promises of their loyalty to Jesus, because Jesus didn't send the promise of his Father upon them yet. They have to wait in Jerusalem until they were endued with power from on high. Holy Spirit is the power they needed to be powerful. Holy Spirit is the teacher they needed to teach. We too trust in the Holy Spirit to witness for Christ. Whether it's internal dangers of hypocrisy or external dangers of persecution, we turn to the Holy Spirit for help When we're in power this way, built together for a dwelling place of God in the Spirit, we can be a city on a hill that cannot be hidden. A spiritual powerhouse. When we trust in the Holy Spirit to witness, we're sound in our invisible structures, and our public faith is impressive in God's sight. Can boldly preach the gospel and even suffer for his name. And today, let's observe the Holy Communion and proclaim the Lord's death till he comes. Let's start with that and let's pray. Lord, there are times when we just wish to be home. We want to be in heaven because life is tough. As we faithfully, or as we strive to be faithful to you, Lord, we face rejection from the world. And even beside external dangers, Lord, we know that sin lurks in us. Though we have power over it, Lord, we won't be removed from its presence until the kingdom comes. Lord, we ask that you give us that power. And as you have told in your scriptures We're thankful that you've given us the Holy Spirit, that we can live for you. May your Spirit work within us, transform us, make us bold, make us fear you above all. Help us to be faithful witness to you, for you, wherever we go. We thank you and we pray all these things in Jesus Christ's name. Amen. Phil's at first.
